summary: John Avery was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Amherst College, University of Tübingen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney. He later served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).

John Borthwick Gilchrist worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Royal High School, George Heriot's School, and the University of Edinburgh, he held posts with the East India Company (~1782–1804), Fort William College (~1800–1804), and East India Company College (1806).
John Brockington is an Indologist who held a post as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh, attested in 1987 and 2003.

John Brough was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Edinburgh under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, University of London, and Cambridge (1967–1984).

John Buescher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America, attested in 2001.
John C. Huntington worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He was a professor at Ohio State University, attested from 1987 to 1990 and in 2000.

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held posts at the University of North Florida, where he is attested in 1988 and as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy in 2015.

John Chadwick was a linguistics, history, and archaeology scholar. He was educated at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1952 to 1984.
John Claude White was active in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He was educated at Rugby School (~1867–1870) and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876).

John Clifford Holt works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1978–2017) and the University of Calgary (2006).
John Collinson Nesfield was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Highgate School and Merton College (~1855–1860).

John Corrigan is a religious studies and history scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1978–1982). He held posts at Harvard (~1982–1984), University of Virginia (~1984–1990), Arizona State University (~1990–2001), and Florida State University (~2001).

John Crook worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sherborne School, Southampton, Jesus College, and under Sheng Yen. He founded the Western Chan Fellowship, held a post at Bristol (1977), and belonged to Université Bouddhique Européenne (~2000–2011).

John D. Dunne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Amherst, CIHTS, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard, he taught at Antioch, CIHTS, Harvard, University of Wisconsin-Madison (1999), and Emory University (~2005–2014).
John Daido Loori was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Taizan Maezumi, whom he succeeded. He served as Abbot at Zen Mountain Monastery from circa 1980 to 2009.
John Daishin Buksbazen is active in Buddhist studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles and under Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman.
John Dowson was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at University College London and as Professor of Hindustani at the Staff College, Camberley (~1855–1877).

John E. Cort is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1982) and Harvard University (~1982–1989), and was appointed Professor at Denison University circa 1993.

John Faithfull Fleet was an Indology and history scholar. Educated at University College London, he served in the Bombay Civil Service and Indian Civil Service (~1867–1897), and as Epigraphist for the Government of India (1883–1886).

John Gombojab Hangin was a linguistics and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana University. He held posts at Johns Hopkins (~1949–1953), Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Indiana University (1964–1989).
